high.title: Banks' Outlook on Profit Growth, Credit Growth, and Capital Mobilization Going Forward
high.summary:
According to a recent SBV survey of credit institutions (CIs), the Vietnamese banking sector reported continued improvement in overall business conditions and pre-tax profits in Q2/2026 versus Q1, though results fell slightly short of prior survey expectations. Looking ahead, **84.1% of CIs expect positive pre-tax profit growth in full-year 2026** versus 2025, while 10.6% anticipate a decline and 5.3% expect no change. Notably, CIs have **revised down their 2026 credit growth forecast to 14.5%** (from 16.0% previously) and **deposit mobilization growth to 14.3%** (from 15.9%), a meaningful downward adjustment of ~1.5–1.6 percentage points each. For Q3/2026 specifically, CIs expect both deposit mobilization and outstanding credit to grow an average of 4.2%. This survey is closely watched as a leading indicator for monetary conditions. The downward revision in credit and deposit growth expectations suggests banks may be anticipating softer loan demand or tighter funding conditions — both relevant for VND liquidity dynamics and potential SBV policy responses. Bond investors should monitor whether slower credit expansion eases upward pressure on lending rates and supports government bond demand.

high.title: Three Scenarios for Vietnamese Equities in July
high.summary: TPS Securities' July strategy report outlines a constructively positive macro backdrop for Vietnamese markets. Key macro highlights directly relevant to FX and rates traders: **USD/VND has remained stable**, and the interest rate environment shows signs of easing pressure — both flagged as foundational conditions for sustained investor confidence. TPS analysts note that exchange rate stability does not directly lift equity prices but serves as a critical prerequisite for a favorable investment environment; when FX risk diminishes, foreign capital is more likely to stay invested. Geopolitical risk reduction in the Middle East is cited as reducing energy price pressure globally, further improving sentiment. Domestically, the government's continued growth-oriented policy stance and positive Q2 GDP momentum underpin the "buy on expectations" phase TPS identifies for July. The three scenarios (bullish, base, and bearish) for the VN-Index hinge predominantly on whether macro stability — particularly on FX and rates — is sustained. For FX and bond traders, the key takeaway is that market consensus currently prices in continued VND stability and no near-term rate hike risk, supporting demand for both equities and fixed income.

high.title: Dragon Capital's Billion-Dollar VEIL Fund Faces Redemption Pressure, May Need to Sell Vietnamese Equities
high.summary: Vietnam Enterprise Investments Limited (VEIL), managed by Dragon Capital and one of the largest foreign funds active on Vietnam's stock market, has announced the results of a tender offer to repurchase up to 10% of its outstanding shares. The outcome reveals significant redemption pressure: shareholders tendered 96.29 million shares — equivalent to a striking 70.06% of total shares outstanding (excluding treasury shares) — far exceeding the 10% buyback limit. Of those, 72.99 million shares were tendered for cash and 23.30 million for an in-kind portfolio transfer. Due to the massive oversubscription, VEIL will allocate on a pro-rata basis, with excess tenders above the basic entitlement accepted at only 1.69%. The repurchase price will be set at the adjusted NAV as of July 8, 2026, less a 2.5% discount, to be announced on July 9.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 8 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary: Entering the second week of July 2026, Vietnamese commercial banks have largely held deposit rates steady with no material adjustments to their online rate schedules. The market remains tiered, with the majority of banks clustering in the 6.6%–6.9% p.a. range for 12-month deposits. The highest posted rate in the system is currently **7.3% p.a. for 12-month tenors at ACB**, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% p.a. ACB also posts 7.2% for 9-month and 7.1% for 6-month tenors. Six banks in total now post rates at or above 7% p.a. for the 12-month bucket: ACB, Saigonbank, MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB. The four large state-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) are implied to remain below this threshold.

medium.title: Dragon Capital Identifies a Market Paradox, Names Two Undervalued Stocks
medium.summary: Dragon Capital's senior equities director published an investor letter noting that **approximately 70% of VN-Index constituents (274 out of 396 stocks) declined in H1/2026**, with only 117 stocks posting gains. The firm attributes broad market weakness to interest rate changes, US-Iran tensions, and general macro uncertainty weighing on investor sentiment. Despite this, Dragon Capital's DCDS fund delivered cumulative returns of over 70% over three years (~19.4% annualized), outperforming the VN-Index's 18.4%. The letter's macro framing — explicitly linking rate changes and geopolitical risk to equity market performance — is relevant context for international fund managers assessing risk-adjusted entry points into Vietnamese equities at current VN-Index levels.

medium.title: A Major Bank Accelerates Dividend Payment and Share Offering
medium.summary:
Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB Bank, ticker: MBB) has announced a Board of Directors resolution to proceed with a capital increase plan through two sequential steps: first, a stock dividend issuance to existing shareholders, followed by a rights offering to existing shareholders via a public share sale. The bank plans to issue approximately 805.5 million shares under the rights offering, targeting gross proceeds of nearly VND 8,055 billion (~USD 315 million). The capital raised will be allocated as follows: VND 3,170 billion for working capital loans to businesses, VND 4,180 billion for project investment and fixed asset lending, and approximately VND 705 billion for retail/personal lending. For VND and equity market participants, this is a meaningful capital event at one of Vietnam's top-tier banks. The rights offering will dilute existing shareholders but strengthens MB's capital adequacy buffer, which is relevant for banking sector credit dynamics and lending capacity. Watch for the record date announcement and any secondary market pressure on MBB shares from dilution concerns.

---

medium.title: New Banking Data Sharing Regulations: All Account Holders to Note Latest Rules on Balance and Transaction Reporting
medium.summary: Effective July 1, 2026, Vietnam's credit institutions and payment intermediaries have entered a new phase of mandatory user data sharing under Decree 252 (implementing the 2025 Tax Administration Law). All domestic banks, foreign bank branches, e-wallets, payment intermediaries, and cross-border payment service providers are now required to periodically report detailed account balance information, transaction histories, and flagged abnormal cash flows directly to tax authorities — a significant expansion from the prior regime, which only required basic identification data. For capital flow monitoring purposes, this regulation enhances the government's visibility into domestic and cross-border fund movements. International fund managers should note that this increased financial surveillance could have implications for capital flow transparency and may affect how foreign entities structure VND-denominated transactions or remittance flows through Vietnamese banking channels.

medium.title: Eight Vietnamese Banks Ranked in Forbes Global 2000 List of World's Largest Public Companies
medium.summary: Eight Vietnamese banks — Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, VPBank, Techcombank, ACB, and HDBank — have been included in the Forbes Global 2000 2026 ranking, representing 8 of Vietnam's 9 total entries (alongside Vingroup). Vietcombank ranks highest at #890 globally with revenue of USD 5.21bn, net profit of USD 1.37bn, total assets of USD 96.84bn, and market cap of USD 19.25bn. BIDV leads on asset size at USD 128.62bn, ranked #967. This recognition underscores the systemic scale and international profile of Vietnam's major state and private banks, which are key components of the VN-Index. For equity investors, the rankings reinforce the investment-grade quality narrative of the large-cap banking sector and may support continued foreign interest in Vietnamese bank stocks.

medium.title: Vietnam's Steel Exports Generate Over Half a Billion USD — Positive Signals from Russia and the U.S.
medium.summary: Vietnam exported approximately 851,000 tonnes of steel in May 2026, generating USD 612 million in export revenue. While export volume declined over 17% month-on-month, the average export price rose to USD 719/tonne — up ~9% from April and ~7% year-on-year — supporting overall revenue stability. For the first five months of 2026, cumulative steel exports reached 4.7 million tonnes worth USD 3 billion, with value up 0.1% versus the same period in 2025. ASEAN remains the dominant export destination, absorbing over 35% of total volumes. Positive demand signals from Russia and the U.S. markets add a modest tailwind. From a macro perspective, robust steel export revenues contribute to Vietnam's trade surplus and support USD inflows, providing a modest positive backdrop for VND stability and the current account balance.

medium.title: State Securities Commission Signs MOU with Two Major Universities to Develop Capital Market Talent
medium.summary: On July 8, 2026, Vietnam's State Securities Commission (SSC) signed Memoranda of Understanding with Foreign Trade University and the Finance Academy, aiming to strengthen human resource development, scientific research, and public education in securities and capital markets. The signing ceremony was attended by SSC Vice Chairman Nguyen Hoang Duong, alongside representatives from the Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (VSDC), the Hanoi Stock Exchange, and industry partners including SSI Securities and FiinGroup. While not a near-term market mover, this initiative reflects regulatory efforts to deepen Vietnam's capital market infrastructure and investor base over the medium term — a positive structural signal for the long-term development of the Vietnamese equity and bond markets.

medium.title: Evening of July 8: Global Gold Prices Reverse Sharply Lower
medium.summary: Global gold prices fell sharply on the evening of July 8, dropping to approximately $4,040/oz — a decline of roughly $140/oz — despite escalating Middle East tensions including attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's refusal to resume peace talks. The article notes a structural shift in gold's safe-haven behavior: geopolitical risk is now being channeled first into crude oil, then into inflation expectations, before impacting monetary policy bets — rather than flowing directly into gold. Investors are also positioning cautiously ahead of the release of the June FOMC minutes. For VND markets, a softening gold price is broadly relevant as Vietnamese domestic gold (SJC) tracks global moves, and sustained gold price weakness could reduce dollarization/gold-hoarding pressures that sometimes weigh on VND sentiment and SBV reserve management.

medium.title: SJC Gold Bar and Plain Gold Ring Prices on the Afternoon of July 8
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices continued their downward correction on July 8, falling VND 500,000–1,200,000/tael for the third consecutive session. SJC gold bars are trading at VND 146.5–149.5 million/tael, while plain gold rings are at VND 146.2–149.2 million/tael (SJC) and VND 144.8–148.8 million/tael (Bao Tin Manh Hai). International spot gold stood at approximately $4,127/oz before pulling back from a $4,190/oz recovery. The article also notes that global central banks — including the PBoC — used last month's dip to accumulate gold reserves. For VND traders, declining domestic gold prices reduce speculative demand for hard assets and may ease pressure on the informal FX market; however, the PBoC's continued gold accumulation is a reminder of broader de-dollarization trends that could influence long-term capital flow dynamics across Asia.
